subtitle: Learn how to connect an organization’s everyday routines to what a person says matters to them, the support they choose, the options actually available and responsible follow-through.
scope: For leaders, managers, supervisors and staff across DHS. Complete original learning examples support private understanding and appropriate practice. They do not determine service eligibility, funding, licensing compliance, accommodation outcomes or allegations. Participation is voluntary. The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads the program and provides guidance, knowledge and feedback while staff do their own work. Actual planning, policy, information, decision and reporting responsibilities remain. Native American and Tribal-specific subjects are referred to the appropriate ADSA office.
introTranscript: A listed activity can be useful without explaining what it supports for a particular person. Follow Dalia’s full example, examine different individually meanings the people describe of support and self-direction, and review a small invented record set. Distinguish an improvement proposal from actual service requirements and role-specific responses. Finish with an honest account of what changed and what remains unknown, through private reflection or appropriate practice.

intro.heading: Connect the person’s purpose to the organization’s work
intro.body:
In an original practice service-planning discussion, Dalia says she wants to learn how to grow herbs and share what she grows with a friend. A draft record lists attendance at the same weekly activity she used last season. Team leader Rowan sees the attendance entry and initially calls the goal supported. Planner Lio asks what the entry establishes: did Dalia choose that activity for this purpose, and does it provide the learning or connection she described? The record does not answer those questions.

Attendance could be useful. The existing activity may offer an opportunity Dalia values, and a familiar arrangement may suit her. It could also be unrelated to the stated purpose or only part of the support. The team should not infer a preference, lack of ambition or rejection of the arrangement from the unanswered record. The inquiry concerns the connection between Dalia’s expressed purpose, the options she understands and the support actually available.

DHS person-centered practices guidance emphasizes listening to what matters to a person, seeing a whole individual and considering supports in that context. This course’s fiction explores that orientation without establishing eligibility, approving a service or promising a funded option. The actual planning and service processes remain relevant. A person-centered question is not permission to omit a requirement or alter someone’s plan without the appropriate process.

Rowan can ask Lio what Dalia understands about the listed activity and which part, if any, she wants to retain. An appropriate conversation can explain the actual available alternatives and limitations, identify a next inquiry and keep Dalia’s choice visible. It should not pressure her to select the option Rowan considers more impressive. The person’s purpose gives the inquiry direction; it does not give a leader control over that person’s decision.

An organizational routine might carry this connection better. For example, a proposed internal review prompt could ask what a listed activity supports and which question remains. That is a proposal to examine, not an immediately adopted planning rule. Use the full example to see what the attendance entry does and does not establish. You may privately recognize why a familiar service looked like a complete answer without changing a real record or producing a live project.

items.title: Keep useful information
items.body: Attendance tells the team that an activity was listed or used. It is not worthless. Retain that information while asking whether it connects to Dalia’s purpose, how she understands it and which choice she makes.

items.title: Do not supply the person’s answer
items.body: Rowan’s interest in a garden activity cannot stand in for Dalia’s preference. An inquiry can make options understandable while leaving room to choose the familiar activity, another available arrangement or an appropriate next question.

items.title: Keep the proposal separate
items.body: Adding a connection prompt is an idea for the actual responsible review. It cannot itself change a service plan, funding, eligibility or the required process. A learning case helps examine the idea without making that change.

tabs.label: Attendance equals purpose
tabs.body: The account treats a listed activity as proof that Dalia’s goal is supported. It may omit her actual understanding and chosen connection. A familiar entry cannot establish those facts by itself.

tabs.label: Replace the activity without asking
tabs.body: Rowan chooses what appears more person-centered and announces it. That substitutes a leader’s judgment for the person’s choice and may promise an unavailable option. The unresolved connection calls for inquiry, not another imposed default.

tabs.label: Examine the connection with the person
tabs.body: The team retains what the record establishes, asks about Dalia’s meaning and explains actual options and limits through the appropriate process. The next account can distinguish a choice, a proposal and an unanswered support question.

check.question: What does the attendance entry establish?
check.correct: An activity is listed; its relationship to Dalia’s purpose and actual choice remains to be examined.
wrong: Dalia necessarily prefers the same activity for every goal.
Rowan may replace the activity without asking because gardening sounds more person-centered.
The listed activity proves every part of the goal has been achieved.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. Retain the entry’s limited information and examine the expressed purpose and actual choice.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A label cannot establish Dalia’s preference or achievement. Replacing it unilaterally repeats the problem; ask about the actual connection and available options.

items.text: Dalia says she wants to learn to grow herbs and share them with a friend.
The draft lists the existing weekly activity.
Ask what part Dalia wants to retain and what it supports.
Explain actual available options and limits through the proper process.
Attendance proves the whole goal has been achieved.
Rowan’s favorite alternative is automatically Dalia’s choice.

intro.heading: Receive different meanings of self-direction and support
intro.body:
In an original practice community workshop, Leni asks to review an activity description with a trusted friend before selecting a session. Organizer Mira initially thinks Leni is surrendering independence. Another participant, Oren, wants to read the description alone and then ask a specific question. Mira calls Oren’s approach the more self-directed one. Neither interpretation examines what the participants say the preparation means.

Leni explains that an earlier shared craft project taught her to test an understanding aloud before choosing. A trusted person can help her notice an unfamiliar term or distinguish an appealing description from the actual arrangement. She wants that discussion; she does not want the friend to answer in her place. Oren explains that an earlier writing group valued forming an initial reading privately before comparing interpretations. Reading first helps Oren hear a later answer without losing the question he already developed.

Mira can now understand both approaches more accurately. The shared discussion may support Leni’s informed choice rather than weaken it. The private reading may serve Oren’s preparation rather than establish superior competence. A suitable workshop invitation can offer the same useful description, allow chosen preparation and make a route for a question clear. The organizer still needs to explain the actual session terms and cannot declare either approach fully effective before examining it.

These are particular learned meanings freely supplied by the people in the example. They do not predict how a family, community, cultural group or disability category prepares decisions. The Council of Europe’s work on personalized affiliations and perspective taking informs the encounter. It does not require Mira to copy an unfamiliar practice or place either participant on an intercultural continuum. Receiving a practical request does not depend on receiving a personal history.

Return to Dalia’s planning case. The team can ask which information and chosen support help her examine the available arrangement while preserving her actual role and applicable representative responsibilities. A companion’s presence is not automatic consent to speaking for her, and working alone is not proof all terms were understood. Your private understanding of why help seemed like dependence may itself be meaningful learning, without a formal assessment, a recorded biography or a live service change.

items.title: Hear Leni’s meaning
items.body: Leni wants to examine terms aloud with a trusted person. She retains the choice. Calling that dependence misses the stated purpose and could remove a useful preparation route rather than improve decision making.

items.title: Hear Oren’s meaning
items.body: Oren values an initial private reading before comparing interpretations. That account explains a preference in this encounter. It does not make every private reader more able or every shared reader less self-directed.

items.title: Offer a route without requiring biography
items.body: Mira can explain the session, allow suitable chosen preparation and answer a practical question without asking anyone to disclose a family story. The supplied histories teach the example; they are not a condition for access.

tabs.label: Rank the preparation styles
tabs.body: Mira treats private reading as a higher level of independence. The ranking ignores Leni’s actual account and does not establish understanding of the session. An organizer’s familiar style is not the measure of another person’s decision.

tabs.label: Let the helper select
tabs.body: Mira assumes the friend can answer because shared preparation was requested. That overstates the permission. Leni asked for a discussion that helps her choose, not for the organizer to replace her decision with someone else’s answer.

tabs.label: Preserve meaning and choice
tabs.body: The invitation allows suitable preparation, retains the same useful information and makes the actual question route understandable. The person’s chosen support and expressed decision remain distinct, with applicable responsibilities intact.

check.question: What should Mira reconsider?
check.correct: Shared examination can support Leni’s own choice, while Oren’s private reading is another particular preparation approach rather than a ranking of people.
wrong: Leni’s community always prefers others to decide.
Oren’s private reading proves a higher intercultural orientation.
Leni must tell the organizer a personal history before reviewing with a friend.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The meanings the people describe widen interpretation while the person’s information, support and decision remain distinct.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Neither account establishes a group script or assessed orientation. Biography cannot be required to answer a practical preparation request; preserve the person’s chosen support and choice.

items.text: Leni values testing a term aloud before selecting.
Oren values an initial private reading before comparison.
Offer useful information and a clear question route.
Retain the person’s expressed choice when support is chosen.
The shared reader has a lower intercultural orientation.
A request for discussion lets the organizer choose for Leni.

responses: Private reading is not a universal test of self-direction.

lessons.transfer: Use Leni and Oren’s complete fiction privately to examine a familiar assumption about help and independence.

move.control: You can receive an individually supplied meaning and reconsider your interpretation.
move.failure: Support is mistaken for surrendered choice or private reading becomes a ranking.
move.next: Explain useful information and chosen preparation while retaining the person’s actual decision role.

intro.heading: Examine whether the record represents the person’s choice
intro.body:
Rowan’s practice team examines ten invented planning records prepared for this learning case. Eight contain the same phrase about attending an activity; two contain different wording. The eight are 80 percent of these ten invented records. That count is accurate, but it does not establish why the phrase recurs, whether every person chose the activity or whether the organization’s real planning is representative of these examples. No actual case files are supplied.

A shared phrase could describe a common chosen activity, a useful standard description or a copied entry that does not carry the person’s purpose clearly. Those possibilities require different follow-up. Rowan should not declare staff uncaring or assume eight people have identical preferences. A small record review can reveal a specific question while leaving its cause and wider extent unknown. It can also retain useful administrative information rather than call every standard phrase meaningless.

The team adds another practice fact: three of the eight entries retain a person’s stated purpose and an explanation of how the activity connects to it. Five do not show that connection. The record now supports a more focused description: five of these ten records leave the connection unexplained in the supplied material. It still does not establish that no conversation occurred, that the service is wrong or that a regulatory violation has been found. An omission from this learning record is not the same thing as an examined person’s actual experience.

A suitable next inquiry asks what the relevant record and person can establish through the actual responsible process. Dalia’s choice may involve a term the record does not explain or a support she wanted to retain. In real work, use the authorized purpose, access roles and information-handling requirements. A course does not authorize a learner to download case files, collect unnecessary identities or publish a small identifiable comparison. Consultant feedback may sharpen the inquiry without replacing staff’s responsibility for it.

Finally, absence of a complaint cannot supply the missing understanding. It may mean many things, including a satisfied person or an unanswered route; the practice material gives no reason. Privately practice a precise account of the count and the question. Meaningful learning does not require a live audit, a new dataset or an employee competence score.

items.title: Use the full denominator
items.body: Eight repeated entries among ten are 80 percent of this practice set. The figure does not describe all people in a program, their preferences or the organization’s current performance. Retain the set’s origin and limit.

items.title: Refine the actual question
items.body: Three repeated entries explain a chosen connection, while five do not. The narrower question concerns the five unexplained connections. It is more useful than treating every similar phrase as proof of failed planning.

items.title: Keep missing reasons unknown
items.body: No complaint is mentioned. That does not establish satisfaction, fear or lack of interest. An appropriate inquiry can examine experience without attaching a reason the material does not provide.

tabs.label: Treat wording as a verdict
tabs.body: The account calls all eight entries proof that staff ignored people. It infers cause and experience from a phrase. The supported observation should prompt a focused inquiry rather than an unsupported character or compliance finding.

tabs.label: Discard the review entirely
tabs.body: The account says a small set cannot reveal anything. It loses a real question in the example. The review can be useful if its scope stays clear and the next inquiry is proportionate.

tabs.label: Describe the gap precisely
tabs.body: Five of the ten practice records do not explain the connection in the supplied material. The team can ask about that gap through appropriate roles while preserving the three explained entries and leaving wider effects unknown.

check.question: What is the most precise account of the practice review?
check.correct: Five of the ten supplied records leave the purpose-to-activity connection unexplained; the cause, actual experience and wider extent remain unknown.
wrong: Eighty percent of all DHS staff ignore the people they serve.
All repeated phrases prove the activities were imposed.
No complaint proves all choices were informed.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The observation becomes useful without an inflated denominator or invented reason.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The records do not measure all DHS staff, imposed choice or informed satisfaction. Retain the actual set and missing connection without inferring cause from wording or silence.

items.text: Eight of ten practice entries repeat a phrase.
Three of the eight explain the connection in the provided material.
What explains the five missing connections?
What does the person understand and choose through the actual process?
Every repeated phrase proves imposed choice.
The absence of a complaint proves informed satisfaction.

move.failure: A missing connection becomes an unsupported cause, universal outcome or person rating.

intro.heading: Keep organizational improvement connected to actual requirements
intro.body:
The practice team proposes adding a short prompt to an internal review discussion: what does the listed activity support, what choice is understood and which question remains? Rowan wants to adopt it immediately for every planning record. Lio asks which actual process the prompt would change and who can consider that change. A helpful idea still needs a clear scope. An internal learning aid is different from an amended service plan, official guidance or a provider requirement.

The linked primary frameworks provide distinct context. DHS describes person-centered practices as considering an individual’s priorities and supports. The federal rule for relevant HCBS waiver planning addresses the person’s direction, understandable information and choice; it also has separate setting and plan requirements. Minnesota section 245D.07 addresses license-holder service planning and delivery within its scope. Minnesota’s Olmstead Implementation Office describes cross-agency goals and currently labels the next plan a draft. None of these sources grants every manager authority to alter funding or turn a new prompt into a compliance finding.

Keep the relevant actual action in view. A proposal for clearer internal review can be examined by its responsible owner. A service-plan question belongs with the actual planning process and applicable requirements. A contract or rate proposal requires its proper authority and review. A setting concern needs the appropriate current examination rather than a classroom declaration that a posted checklist proves compliance or that four similar schedules prove a violation. The person’s actual choices and the available evidence still matter.

In the example, Dalia asks whether a different gardening session is available. The team can seek the actual terms and explain what is known. It cannot promise a newly paid unit because the course favors it, cancel the existing arrangement without the appropriate process or infer that a familiar choice is less valuable. A proposed opportunity may be worth pursuing while remaining unavailable or undecided today.

Use the source links for their stated scope and consult the relevant current guidance through actual responsible roles in real work. This course does not teach every regulation, adopt a draft plan or decide a case. Your private understanding of why an appealing idea felt like authority can improve how you distinguish proposal, approval and actual effect. No live contract change or required service redesign is a condition of that learning.

items.title: An internal prompt has a limited purpose
items.body: The practice prompt can make a review question clearer. It is not automatically an amendment to service planning, licensing guidance or funding. Identify what the proposal changes and seek its actual responsible consideration.

items.title: The person’s choice is not a generic outcome
items.body: A gardening idea does not become Dalia’s preference just because it sounds attractive. Ask about the actual option, its terms and her understanding. Preserve current responsibilities rather than promise a service through the course.

items.title: Use current sources at their scope
items.body: A state planning draft and a current service requirement are different. The source links support examining those distinctions; they do not make the lesson an official determination or replace actual legal, licensing or policy review.

tabs.label: Promise a new paid unit
tabs.body: Rowan announces an additional funded option on the strength of the learning exercise. A course cannot establish availability, funding or authority. A worthwhile proposal still needs the appropriate process and honest current status.

tabs.label: Treat a checklist as the whole finding
tabs.body: The team reports universal compliance from posted items without examining the actual applicable requirements and person’s experience. A limited observation can inform review but does not settle every setting or plan question.

tabs.label: Keep scope and actual next review clear
tabs.body: The account names the proposed prompt, distinguishes it from service decisions and explains which actual responsibility will consider it. Dalia receives what is known about options rather than a premature promise.

check.question: What can the learning prompt establish?
check.correct: A clearer proposed inquiry whose actual use must fit the relevant requirements and decision responsibility; it does not itself approve a service, funding or compliance finding.
wrong: Automatic authority to alter every provider contract.
Proof that any repeated schedule violates every applicable rule.
Adoption of the next Olmstead Plan because the course links the draft.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. Useful inquiry and actual authority remain connected but distinct.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The lesson cannot supply contract authority, a universal legal finding or adoption of a draft plan. Identify the actual action and current responsible review.

The Olmstead office labels the next plan a draft.

Explore the actual terms of another gardening opportunity.

A familiar schedule alone proves universal noncompliance.

responses: The learning case does not establish funding or unlimited availability.

intro.heading: Support improvement without delaying a required response
intro.body:
Rowan’s practice staff team is discussing whether an internal review prompt helps people explain the link between a goal and an activity. In a separate conversation, employee Jess says a disability-related medical condition makes the present meeting time difficult and asks for a change. Rowan wants the group to consider the whole issue as a person-centered design exercise. That would confuse an ordinary improvement idea with a separate accommodation request.

MMB Policy 1433 does not require a requestor to use a special label. The recipient should promptly forward the request to the appropriate decision-maker and at the same time tell the requestor who that decision-maker is. Supervisors and managers must not request medical information or documentation; appropriate documentation requests belong to the agency ADA Coordinator. Actual confidentiality and need-to-know responsibilities remain. A group should not ask Jess to explain a diagnosis as part of its learning discussion.

An optional discussion may examine general meeting preparation without deciding Jess’s request or replacing the assigned process. Rowan cannot promise the requested outcome merely because the course encourages a wider perspective. Rowan also cannot delay forwarding until the team reaches consensus. The appropriate process can clarify responsibilities and the request while the learning remains separate.

Another separate practice event concerns employee Nia, who reports protected-class insulting remarks to supervisor Rowan. MMB Policy 1436 requires managers and supervisors to immediately report all such allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow agency procedures. Rowan does not first decide whether the allegation is proven, seek a workshop solution or wait for consultant feedback. The actual process examines the allegation; this course makes no finding or promise of discipline.

The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads program guidance, knowledge and feedback while staff do their own equity work. That support can improve the team’s questions without becoming permission to use a resource or a prerequisite to a required response. Native American and Tribal-specific subjects are referred to the appropriate ADSA office rather than taught here. Use these complete practice distinctions privately or in appropriate practice. Do not enter live allegations, personal medical material or case records into the learning exercise.

items.title: Recognize the ordinary request
items.body: Jess’s words identify a disability-related work adjustment request. A special course label is unnecessary. Prompt forwarding and simultaneous identification of the decision-maker preserve the actual receiving responsibility without promising the outcome.

items.title: Keep medical handling out of the learning group
items.body: The exercise does not authorize supervisors or managers to request medical information or documentation. The agency ADA Coordinator handles appropriate requests through the actual process. Work-relevant need-to-know duties do not become public disclosure to a class.

items.title: Report the allegation immediately
items.body: Nia reports a protected-class allegation to a supervisor. Rowan immediately reports it to HR or the agency AAO and follows agency procedures. A finding is not a prerequisite, and optional team learning or consultant feedback cannot delay the report.

tabs.label: Let the learning group decide
tabs.body: The group votes on Jess’s request or whether Nia’s report deserves a referral. That substitutes a classroom activity for assigned processes. The actual request and immediate manager duty remain regardless of a vote.

tabs.label: Promise the result
tabs.body: Rowan assures Jess of a specific adjustment or Nia of a disciplinary finding because the course favors inclusive practice. Those outcomes belong to the actual process. Support should preserve responsibilities without guaranteeing an unexamined decision.

tabs.label: Respond through the actual roles
tabs.body: Rowan promptly forwards the request and identifies its decision-maker, protects appropriate medical handling and immediately reports the separate allegation. General learning can continue without delaying, adjudicating or exposing these matters.

image.caption: Four people stand in a hallway holding folders, papers and a laptop.

intro.heading: Review what changed without turning activity into success
intro.body:
In the complete practice follow-up, the appropriate owner agrees to test the short internal review prompt in a learning discussion. The discussion now retains Dalia’s herb-growing purpose instead of reporting only activity attendance. Lio explains that the existing activity includes one relevant demonstration, but the terms of another session remain unverified. Dalia says she wants to keep that demonstration and asks for a clearer explanation of the alternative before deciding whether to change anything.

The supplied result is useful and limited. The discussion retains Dalia’s expressed purpose, a specific connection and her current preference. It has not demonstrated that she grew herbs, shared them with a friend or received a newly funded service. Nor has the new prompt established every person’s experience, the organization’s overall performance or the team’s intercultural orientation. Use the result for what it actually supports rather than protect an attractive success story.

A next appropriate inquiry can seek the alternative’s actual terms, preserve the chosen current part and explain how the answer will reach Dalia through the real planning process. The team should not infer that her unanswered question means dissatisfaction or that her preference for the existing demonstration means she rejected change. A person can value a familiar part and still want clearer options. Follow-through includes preserving that meaning as information moves between responsible roles.

The review also notices a weakness: one practice summary calls all planning person-centered because the prompt was used. Rowan corrects the account to name the particular connection clarified and the outstanding term. A process count might help describe use of a prompt, but it cannot by itself measure a person’s informed choice or meaningful outcome. Any real information review needs its authorized purpose and handling requirements; the course does not create a new reporting system.

You can finish by understanding why a service label, chosen help or a copied phrase had a broader meaning than you first gave it. The Leni/Oren encounter may widen your sense of self-direction, while Dalia’s complete case may change the question you would ask. That private learning is legitimate without an immediate workplace product, a manager deadline or proof of improvement in someone else’s life. Appropriate application can follow when a real task and actual responsibility call for it.

items.title: Name the useful result
items.body: The discussion now connects the existing demonstration with a part Dalia wants to retain. That is progress in the example. It should not be lost because another option remains unclear, nor expanded into proof her whole goal was achieved.

items.title: Carry the unresolved term forward
items.body: The next account retains the alternative question and actual responsibility for seeking its terms. A reader should not have to reconstruct the question from a vanished note or infer that a completed prompt means all choices are understood.

items.title: Correct the broader claim
items.body: Calling all planning person-centered from one prompt overstates the result. Correct it to the particular connection and known limits. Honest correction can retain the useful change without a universal success or failure statement.

tabs.label: Count the prompt as the outcome
tabs.body: The report says every personal goal improved because the prompt was used. It confuses organizational activity with an examined effect and loses the unverified term. A usage count cannot supply the person’s understanding or later experience.

tabs.label: Call every part unsuccessful
tabs.body: The report discards Dalia’s expressed preference and the demonstrated connection because the alternative remains open. That erases supported progress. An accurate account can preserve both the useful result and unfinished inquiry.

tabs.label: Retain progress and the next question
tabs.body: The report names the chosen demonstration, Dalia’s purpose, the unverified alternative term and how the next appropriate answer will be obtained. It does not pretend a service or later outcome has already been delivered.

check.question: What does the follow-up support?
check.correct: The discussion better preserves Dalia’s purpose and current chosen connection, while the alternative’s terms and later personal outcomes remain unexamined.
wrong: Every DHS service is now person-centered because a prompt was tested.
Dalia achieved the entire goal when the record mentioned herbs.
The unresolved alternative means no useful learning occurred.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The actual result remains useful without claiming more than the example establishes.
check.feedbackIncorrect: One prompt cannot describe every service, a recorded purpose is not an achieved goal, and an open term does not erase supported progress. Keep the particular change and remaining inquiry together.

items.text: The discussion retains Dalia’s expressed herb-growing purpose.
Dalia wants to retain a particular existing demonstration.
The alternative session’s terms remain unverified.
Later herb growing and sharing have not been examined.
One prompt proves every DHS service improved.
Mentioning the purpose proves Dalia achieved the whole goal.

options: Keep the universal claim to show commitment.

This preserves useful progress and follow-through without a false assurance.
An open question does not negate the supplied useful result.

move.control: You can describe progress and the unfinished question accurately.
move.failure: Using a prompt becomes a universal success measure or unresolved terms erase useful learning.

remember: A service or activity label is not the person’s whole purpose.

sections.heading: Examine the person’s connection
items: What has this person actually said matters?
How does the activity relate to that purpose, and what remains unexplained?
Explain actual options and limits without deciding the person’s preference.
Preserve chosen support, expressed choice and applicable representative responsibilities.

sections.heading: Keep evidence proportionate
items: State the supplied set and denominator; do not turn it into an agency-wide result.
A repeated phrase is an inquiry rather than proof of a cause.
The absence of a complaint does not establish understanding or satisfaction.
Real inquiry follows authorized purpose, information access and handling roles.

sections.heading: Preserve actual requirements
items: An internal learning prompt does not amend a plan, contract, funding rule or license.
Use current primary sources at the action and role they address.
A draft plan remains a draft; a limited checklist is not every compliance finding.
Seek appropriate actual review and preserve required equity analysis for qualifying actions.

sections.heading: Carry role-specific responses
items: Promptly forward an accommodation request and at the same time tell the requestor who the appropriate decision-maker is.
Supervisors and managers must not request medical information or documentation; appropriate requests belong to the agency ADA Coordinator.
Keep actual confidentiality and need-to-know requirements; do not use personal medical material in learning.
Managers and supervisors immediately report all protected-class allegations or incidents to HR or the agency AAO and follow agency procedures.
Optional learning and consultant feedback cannot delay these responses or promise their outcomes.
Refer Native American and Tribal-specific subjects to the appropriate ADSA office.

sections.heading: Follow through honestly
items: Retain the particular chosen connection and supported progress.
Carry the remaining term or inquiry into the next appropriate account.
Using a prompt does not by itself establish a personal outcome.
Use the full example or private understanding without a compulsory real redesign, staff rating or submission.
